goal: Implement SPEC.md F12 with a local GPU backend that runs without automated content screening.
acceptance: The CLI and GUI use the local GHOST backend for scan, pick, swap, retry, and resume. No explicit-content classifier or screening weight is invoked. The app retains explicit operator consent and non-explicit attestations, non-overwrite and failure behavior, 720p output, first audio track, original timing, visible AI-ALTERED labeling, GPU-only inference, and compatible fresh job state. Actual CUDA CLI and GUI scan/conversion runs on synthetic AI-generated adult-face media verify frame count/rate, retained audio, visible label, metadata, and a localized face-region pixel change beyond source-video encoding noise. ONNX Runtime session creation is instrumented to allow only the five pinned models and requires CUDA for every session; content-screening modules must remain unloaded. Unit tests cover index/time selection, retry/resume orchestration, and retention of progress after a failed CUDA setup retry. A failed conversion publishes no output. No real-person media is authorized or required. GPU retry/resume success, clean-install behavior, real-person identity quality, long-video stability, Linux behavior, and other untested levels remain NOT_VERIFIED.
owner_approval: The owner explicitly requested removal of automated content supervision from conversion and authorized implementing the replacement backend. The owner approved downloading GHOST and CrossFace weights for personal non-commercial research, directed use of synthetic media only, and authorized revising docs/REVIEWER.md and F12 acceptance criteria to match the no-screening scope. Upstream FaceFusion source remains untouched.
boundaries: Follow docs/SPEC.md F12 and acceptance criteria
Preserve upstream-facefusion at its pinned, clean revision. Implement the owner-approved no-screening requirement in the separate backend without modifying upstream source.
No GPU rental, model download, face-processing service, or use of personal media without explicit approval of exact assets, size, cost, and reason.
Keep generated media, model files, credentials, and private paths out of Git and logs.
Update the F12 checklist and acceptance only as explicitly authorized by the owner; do not weaken unrelated contracts, tests, requirements, or review gates.
